## Verdict: converging, with one real defect

The mathematics of this session is genuine and the reduction is real, but the theorem that was shipped is not the theorem the reduction licenses. Not churn, not sorry-stall: nine new declarations, all kernel-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, both files elaborate green, and no sorry or axiom was added anywhere. One binder is wrong, and it is the binder the whole claim rests on.

A parallel reviewer reached the central finding independently and filed it first (I-0591, I-0593, I-0592). I confirmed it separately and added one measurement they did not have. My duplicate is archived; the delta is a comment on I-0591.

## Answers to the six questions

**1. The reduction is lossless. The shipped theorem is not.** `hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean:267`) is correct in both directions. `SymPowData.isColimit`'s `uniq` field is real — it is `D.desc(...).choose_spec.2 u (hu (SingleObj.star _))`, the genuine `∃!` uniqueness component, not a `Subsingleton` collapse, and the one-object index category makes `hu` at the single star sufficient rather than weaker.

The defect is downstream. The iff is about **one** diagram, `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)`. `exists_unique_albanese_of_scheme_colimits` assumes `HasColimitsOfShape (SingleObj (Equiv.Perm (Fin g))) Scheme` — every diagram of that shape in all of `Scheme`. Its docstring (`AlbaneseFromColimit.lean:67-70`) claims that hypothesis "is equivalent — not merely sufficient — to the datum previously assumed (`hasColimit_permDiagram_iff`)". That is false. Measured: blanket ⟹ single synthesizes; single ⟹ blanket fails. And the capstone restated with `[HasColimit (permDiagram C g)]` compiles with the proof term untouched, so the larger binder was never needed. One-line fix at `AlbaneseFromColimit.lean:75`, same at `SymPowColimit.lean:428`.

**2. `symPowData_affine` is a correct theorem; two of its three prose claims are unproved.** The `letI := ofHasFiniteProducts` is inert and harmless — `permAut`, `SymPowData`, `permDiagram` and `symPowData_of_hasColimit` all carry only `[HasFiniteProducts]`, never `[CartesianMonoidalCategory]`, so your product-mismatch worry does not bite. But `(Under k)ᵒᵖ` is k-algebras-op; nothing in the file connects it to `AffineScheme` or `Scheme.Spec`, and the "colimit is `Spec (A^{⊗n})^{S_n}`" identification is docstring only. `mem_sections_singleObj_iff` never mentions `CommRingCat`, `Spec`, `Under k`, or a tensor power — it is a generic sections-are-invariants lemma, and mathlib already has `SingleObj.Types.sections.equivFixedPoints`. Your own §6 disclaimer at `:433-440` states this correctly; §5 at `:338` and `:357-361` asserts the stronger reading anyway, and that stronger text was propagated verbatim to `SymPowInterface.lean:98-100` and `AlbaneseUP.lean:96-98` where the disclaimer is absent.

**3. `permAut_swap_ne_id` is proved, and it does not cover the application.** Correct at `Type`/`Bool`/`n=2`. But the generalisation in `symPowDataTrivial`'s docstring (`SymPowInterface.lean:288`, "would force `permAut C σ = 𝟙`") is false. I proved the counter-direction: at a **terminal** object `permAut C σ = 𝟙` for all `n`, so `symPowDataTrivial` satisfies `hproj` at every `n` there. No scheme is exhibited anywhere with `permAut ≠ 𝟙`. Nobody will instantiate at a terminal curve, but the non-vacuity *argument* as written does not reach `Over (Spec k̄)`. One lemma closes it. Filed as I-0596.

**4. `permEnd` is correct.** `map_mul'` proves `permAut C (σ*τ)⁻¹ ≫ π = (permAut C τ⁻¹ ≫ permAut C σ⁻¹) ≫ π`, which is `End`'s `f * g = g ≫ f` with the inversion exactly compensating. `permAut_eq_map` (`:130`) recovers `permAut C σ` at index `σ⁻¹` via `inv_inv`, so the symmetry statement quantifies over all of `S_n` with no loss. No off-by-inversion weakening.

**5. It really takes no `SymPowData` and no `hproj`, and it is genuinely III.6.1** — the body delegates to `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation_of_birational` with `symPowOfColimit C g` and `symPowOfColimit_proj_perm C g` supplied, and the other 16 binders are character-identical to the sibling at `AlbaneseFromData.lean:438-460`. `[IsReduced ((symPowOfColimit C g).carrier).left]` and `hover` are inherited unchanged, not new demands.

The vacuity question has a sharper answer than either reviewer gave. **The residue is satisfiable at g ≤ 1 and unsatisfiable at g ≥ 2.** `Equiv.Perm (Fin 1)` is a subsingleton, so every `SingleObj` diagram over it is its own colimit via the identity cocone — I built the blanket instance at g=1 and it is axiom-clean. That is the worse case, not the better one: a uniformly vacuous hypothesis is inert and cannot be misreported, but this one can be discharged in a few lines, axiom-clean, at precisely the g your own `SymPowInterface.lean:74-78` warns must not be cited as evidence the group law is exercised. That is why the one-binder fix is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
